about: What tools/Rebake-Packs.mjs downloads and how it bakes each pack (docs/BAKING.md). Every option was established by reproducing the published packs (tools/packs.json) byte for byte, first on 17 November 2026; each product's "why" says where each option comes from. A body's pack version (its folder, <body>-vN) is the app's own table, web/pack-base.js. "manifests" holds the SHA-256 of each published manifest with its wall time (bake.seconds) and its sources' download dates removed, keys sorted, as the script compares them.

why.no-data (the default): The file's own GDAL no-data tag (0 in this image) is read: a pixel of that value is a hole, baked mid grey, as Venus, Pluto and Charon were. Version 1 (31 October 2026, before 21:00) was baked before the baker read the tag, so its holes are black; `--no-data none` reproduces it. Version 2 (17 November 2026) corrects it.

why.--height-scale 0.5: 0.5 m per unit, as the product states (GeoTIFF metadata SCALE 0.5, ISIS label Multiplier 0.5). Version 1 was baked at 1, found by matching its bytes (every page's height offset and step exactly twice), so its relief was twice the measured relief; version 2 (17 November 2026) corrects it.
why.height no-data: The elevation file holds no -32768 cell, so reading its tag or not changes nothing.
why.no decimation: The impostor map, which depends only on the image and its decimation, matches at 1.

why.height scale 1 (the default): MOLA heights are whole metres above the areoid (ISIS label Multiplier 1.0; the GeoTIFF states no scale). Matches the published bytes.
why.height no-data: The elevation file holds no -32768 cell, so its tag changes nothing.

products.name: moon
products.credit: LRO LROC WAC and LOLA, NASA/GSFC/ASU, NASA/JPL, USGS Astrogeology

why.no-data (the default): The file's own GDAL no-data tag (0 in this image) is read, as for every body. The image holds no such pixel, so version 1, baked on 31 October 2026 before the baker read the tag, is unchanged by it.
why.--decimate-image 2: The 109164 x 54582 mosaic is averaged 2 x 2 as it is read: whole, its accumulators would need about 70 GB. Found by reproducing the published impostor map, which depends only on the image and this factor (3 does not match).
why.--decimate-height 2: The 92160 x 46080 elevation model, averaged 2 x 2 as it is read. Found by matching the published pages.
why.--height-scale 0.5: 0.5 m per unit, as the product states (GeoTIFF metadata SCALE 0.5, ISIS label Multiplier 0.5, product page: elevation = DN * 0.5). The published pages confirm it: at scale 1 every page's offset and step double.
why.height no-data: The elevation file holds no -32768 cell, so its tag changes nothing.

why.options: As recorded in the published Earth manifest (bake): JPEG quality 88, 4:4:4, height step 1 m, page step up to 16 m at roughness / 4, 15 zopfli iterations. These are also the defaults.

why.map --jpeg: The whole Blue Marble August 2004 image, area-averaged to 1024 x 512. Matches the published bytes.
PIA07782.jpg, the cylindrical map of Cassini's December 2000 flyby; proven by reproducing the published bytes.

why.starmap_2020_8k.exr: The 8192 x 4096 map (the 4k one was fetched first and replaced): the cube is 2048 per face, the map's own density at its equator. The catalogue only checks the orientation. Matches the published bytes.

why.--faintest 4.5: The 906 stars brighter than magnitude 4.5. Matches the published bytes.

why.recorded query: The answer saved on 31 October 2026 reproduces the published bytes; a live answer does not.

why.copy: The published file is byte-identical to the fit kept in the repository.
why.--ephemeris-from-kernels: solar-bake solar on these ten NAIF kernels reproduces the same bytes (checked 17 November 2026 with the copies downloaded on 31 October, which NAIF still serves at the same sizes).
